What makes contract & private-label manufacturing different

  • New brand enquiries from marketplaces and referrals need fast, informed replies on MOQ, formats and timelines.

  • Sample and artwork rounds are tracked in chats and spreadsheets, so projects stall without a clear next owner.

  • Packaging and client-supplied materials arrive late and stop production runs that were already scheduled.

  • Brand owners expect complaint responses, CAPA evidence and release dates they can pass on to their own customers.

Where automation helps contract & private-label manufacturing

  • Brand enquiry intake

    Capture third-party manufacturing enquiries from IndiaMART, the website and referrals with product type, format, MOQ and timeline, and route them to the right business development owner.

  • Consistent costing for brand quotes

    Draft quotes from formulation or BOM costs, packaging options and MOQ breaks for the costing lead to correct and approve.

  • Shared sample and artwork portal

    Track samples, feedback rounds, label declaration checks and artwork approvals with each brand client in one place, with a named approver for every sign-off.

  • Packaging and client-supplied material follow-ups

    Chase suppliers and clients on open POs and promised material dates, and flag shortages against the production plan before the run is due.

  • Complaint and CAPA reporting for brand owners

    Route brand-owner complaints to QA with batch details, track CAPA actions, and draft responses for QA approval.

  • Release-expected view for clients

    Show brand clients which batches are pending release and what is outstanding, without exposing GxP record content.

Enquiry & qualificationStandard3–5 weeks

Marketplace and website enquiry capture with routing

Pull every enquiry from IndiaMART, TradeIndia, the website and the RFQ inbox into one CRM queue, remove duplicates, extract what the buyer needs and route it to the right product or territory owner with a response deadline.

Industrial & engineering manufacturers · Process, chemical & pharma manufacturing · Contract & private-label manufacturing

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Enquiries arrive through marketplace dashboards, email, website forms, phone calls and trade-fair cards. Sales coordinators copy them by hand, duplicates from the same buyer go to two reps, and enquiries that arrive after hours wait until someone notices them. Buyers who send the same RFQ to several suppliers often shortlist whoever replies first with a sensible question.

Trigger

A new lead appears through the IndiaMART Lead Manager API, a marketplace or website form notification arrives, or an email lands in the shared RFQ inbox.

How it runs

  1. Collect leads from the IndiaMART Lead Manager API, other marketplace notifications, website forms and the RFQ mailbox into one queue.
  2. Normalize names, phone numbers, company names and GSTIN where given, then match against existing CRM accounts and open enquiries to avoid duplicate follow-up.
  3. Use an AI model to extract product, grade or specification, quantity, delivery location, required date and attachments, and list missing information as questions for the rep.
  4. Score fit against agreed rules such as product range, minimum order, serviceable region and buyer type, and route to the product or territory owner with a response deadline.
  5. Send an acknowledgement by email, or by WhatsApp only where the buyer started the chat or opted in, and alert the owner in Slack or the CRM app.
  6. Escalate enquiries with no human response by the deadline to the sales coordinator.

Human checkpoint

The sales coordinator reviews low-confidence extractions, out-of-territory enquiries and anything flagged as a large or strategic account before routing. Reps qualify every enquiry by call or email; the automation never sends prices or delivery commitments.

Systems it connects

  • IndiaMART Lead Manager API
  • TradeIndia and other B2B marketplaces
  • Website forms and RFQ mailbox
  • CRM such as Zoho CRM, HubSpot or Salesforce

Data & consent

Uses the business contact details and enquiry content the buyer submitted. Only fields needed for qualification are kept in the CRM; raw marketplace payloads are held for a short agreed period for troubleshooting, then deleted. Promotional messages go only to contacts who agreed to receive them. Access follows CRM roles.

What we deliver

  • Unified enquiry queue in the CRM
  • Extraction and routing rules with confidence thresholds
  • Response-time and source dashboard
  • Escalation alerts for unowned enquiries

How we measure it

  • Enquiry first-response time
  • Duplicate enquiry rate
  • Enquiries without an owner after the deadline
  • Qualified enquiries by source

Specification, samples & quoteAdvanced6–10 weeks

RFQ-to-quote drafting with estimator approval

Turn RFQ emails, drawings and BOQs into a structured costing draft based on your item master, past quotes and current rates, so the estimator reviews and approves a quote instead of building it from scratch, and the eventual PO is checked against it.

Industrial & engineering manufacturers · Contract & private-label manufacturing

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Quoting depends on one or two experienced estimators who rebuild costing sheets in Excel for every RFQ, look up old quotes from memory and chase purchase for current material rates. Turnaround slips when they are on the shop floor or traveling, assumptions are not recorded, and the same part can be priced differently for different buyers.

Trigger

An enquiry is marked qualified in the CRM with an RFQ, drawing, specification sheet, formulation brief or BOQ attached.

How it runs

  1. Extract line items, material grade, quantity breaks, finish, packing and delivery terms from the RFQ, BOQ and drawing title blocks and notes, flagging any dimension or tolerance it cannot read with confidence.
  2. Match each line to the item master, released drawing revisions where the PDM exposes an API or export, and similar past quotes, and show what changed since the last quote to this buyer.
  3. Pull current raw material rates, machine-hour or conversion rates, tooling and freight assumptions from the rate tables maintained by purchase and costing.
  4. Generate a costing sheet and quote draft in the standard template, with assumptions, deviations from the buyer's specification and open technical questions listed.
  5. Route the draft to the estimator in a review screen; discounts beyond the agreed matrix go to the sales head for approval.
  6. Send the approved quote as a PDF from the rep's address, log the version in the CRM, schedule follow-ups and capture win or loss reasons at close.
  7. When the buyer's PO arrives, compare price, quantity, delivery and terms with the approved quote and stage a draft sales order for the commercial manager.

Human checkpoint

The estimator or applications engineer checks every technical interpretation, cost element and price before release, and the sales head approves discounts outside the matrix. Nothing reaches a buyer without a named approver recorded against that quote version.

Systems it connects

  • ERP item master and price lists
  • Costing sheets and rate tables
  • CAD/PDM drawing repository

Data & consent

Uses buyer RFQs and drawings, which may be confidential or under NDA, plus internal costs and margins. Documents are processed under API terms that exclude training on client data, in a region the client approves where the provider offers one, with access limited to sales, estimation and management. Margin fields are hidden from roles that do not need them, and files follow the client's document retention policy.

What we deliver

  • Structured RFQ extraction with confidence flags
  • Costing draft and quote generator in the standard template
  • Estimator review and approval screen
  • Quote register with versions, approvals and win or loss reasons
  • PO-to-quote comparison with draft sales order

How we measure it

  • Quote turnaround time
  • Quote-to-order conversion
  • Quotes revised after buyer queries
  • Estimator time per quote

Specification, samples & quoteStandard5–7 weeks

Private-label sample, artwork and approval tracking

Track each brand client's brief, samples, feedback rounds, artwork and label approvals and first-order readiness in one shared portal, so both sides can see what is pending and who must act next.

Contract & private-label manufacturing

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Contract manufacturers run many brand projects at once. Briefs arrive on WhatsApp, sample versions are tracked in a spreadsheet, feedback is scattered across calls and chats, and artwork goes through several rounds before anyone checks the mandatory label declarations. Projects stall because nobody knows whether the client or the factory owes the next step.

Trigger

A new brand client brief is accepted, a sample is dispatched, client feedback arrives, or an artwork version is uploaded.

How it runs

  1. Capture the brief in a structured form: product type, specification or formulation targets, pack format, MOQ, target cost and timeline.
  2. Create a project with stages for samples, feedback, stability or testing, artwork, label approval and first order, each with an owner and due date.
  3. Log each sample version with its R&D or QA release, courier tracking and client feedback, keeping a full version history.
  4. Run each artwork version through a mandatory-declarations checklist for the product category before the client sees it, and record the client's named approver and approval date.
  5. Notify the next owner when a stage completes, send weekly status to the client contact, and convert approved projects into a sales order and BOM request.

Human checkpoint

R&D or QA releases each sample. The manufacturer's regulatory or QA owner confirms label declarations for the product category, such as Legal Metrology, FSSAI, cosmetics or drug labeling rules. The brand client's named approver signs off artwork in the portal before printing.

Plan, procure, make & checkStarter2–4 weeks

Supplier PO follow-ups and inbound material tracking

Follow up open purchase orders before their due dates, read supplier replies into expected dates for the buyer to confirm, and flag shortages against the production plan or dealer backorders.

Distributors & dealer networks · Contract & private-label manufacturing

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Buyers chase suppliers and principals by phone and email for every open PO. Revised dates stay in inboxes, planning learns about a packaging or raw material shortage on the day of production, and distributors discover a principal's short supply only when dealers complain.

Trigger

An open PO line approaches its due date, a supplier replies to a follow-up, or a goods receipt differs from the PO.

How it runs

  1. Read open PO lines, due dates and supplier contacts from the ERP every morning.
  2. Send templated follow-up emails before and on the due date from the buyer's mailbox or a shared purchase address.
  3. Use AI to read supplier replies for committed dates, partial quantities and issues, and propose updated expected dates for the buyer to confirm.
  4. Compare expected receipts with the production plan or dealer backorders and flag shortages to planning or sales.
  5. Flag goods receipt mismatches, and alert accounts as invoices from registered micro or small suppliers near the MSMED Act payment deadline, which cannot exceed 45 days from acceptance.

Human checkpoint

The buyer confirms every revised date before it reaches planning. Changes to PO price, quantity or supplier are made only by the purchase manager in the ERP. Shortfalls of client-supplied material are raised with the brand client by the account manager.

  • Production plan or MRP

Plan, procure, make & checkStandard4–6 weeks

Quality NCR, customer complaint and CAPA routing

Raise non-conformances and customer complaints with photos, lot and part details, route them to the right quality owner, track containment and CAPA actions to closure, and draft 8D reports for QA approval.

Industrial & engineering manufacturers · Contract & private-label manufacturing

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

NCRs are raised on paper or by email, containment depends on who remembers, and CAPA due dates slip between shifts. OEM customers and brand owners expect 8D reports and evidence of effectiveness checks, but the quality team spends days compiling them from scattered photos, test results and email threads.

Trigger

An inspector logs a non-conformance at incoming, in-process or final inspection, or a customer complaint arrives by email, portal or through the account manager.

How it runs

  1. Capture the NCR with part or product, drawing revision, batch or lot, quantity, defect type and photos through a mobile form.
  2. Assign a number, route it to the QA owner for that product line and open containment tasks with due dates.
  3. Show similar past NCRs and their root causes, and draft a structured 5-why or 8D outline from the record for the quality engineer to complete.
  4. Track corrective and preventive actions, send reminders before due dates and schedule effectiveness checks.
  5. Compile the customer-facing 8D or complaint response from approved content for QA sign-off.

Human checkpoint

The QA manager decides disposition (use as is, rework, scrap or return) and approves root cause, CAPA closure and every customer-facing report. AI output is marked as draft and never closes a record. On GxP sites, deviations and CAPAs stay in the validated QMS.

Plan, procure, make & checkAdvanced5–8 weeks

Batch release readiness tracker around validated systems

Show, for every batch, whether production records, QC tests, deviations and documents are complete by reading status from validated systems, and remind the right reviewers, without touching the GxP record itself.

Process, chemical & pharma manufacturing · Contract & private-label manufacturing

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Finished batches wait in quarantine while QA chases missing signatures, pending QC tests, open deviations and CoA drafts across separate systems and paper records. Planning and sales cannot tell when stock will be released, so they call QA repeatedly, and brand clients ask for status the plant cannot easily give.

Trigger

A batch is completed in the ERP or MES, or the status of a QC test, deviation or batch record review changes in its source system.

How it runs

  1. Read batch status, QC test status from the LIMS, open deviations from the QMS and batch record review status through read-only exports or reports.
  2. Show a readiness board per batch listing what is complete, what is pending and the responsible reviewer.
  3. Send reminders to reviewers for overdue items and a daily summary of batches expected to be ready for the release decision.
  4. Give planning, sales and brand clients a release-expected view without exposing GxP record content.

Human checkpoint

Only QA releases or rejects a batch, following site SOPs in the validated systems. The tracker is a read-only, non-GxP reporting layer introduced through the site's change control, and it never creates, edits or approves a GxP record or signature.

Tools

PPythonSSupabaseRRetoolnn8nSSlack

Systems it connects

  • LIMS such as LabWare or STARLIMS
  • QMS for deviations and CAPA
  • ERP or MES batch records
  • Batch record review log

Data & consent

Batch and test status data only. The tracker copies just the status fields needed for reminders, with timestamps and source references, and refreshes rather than edits them. Access is role-based, brand clients see only their own batches, and retention follows the site's document control policy.

What we deliver

  • Read-only status integration with LIMS, QMS and ERP
  • Batch readiness board
  • Reviewer reminders and daily summary
  • Release-expected view for planning and clients

How we measure it

  • Batch completion to release time
  • Batches waiting on a single pending item
  • Overdue review items
  • Release date queries to QA
